subject: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@amarisplc.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris

Hi Tara,

Thanks again for taking time last week. Per our conversation, Amaris is up for contract renewal on 2027-07-01 and you mentioned interest in a 12–18 month extension tied to a step-up in committed capacity (roughly +30% starting Q4). I wanted to capture three pragmatic commercial paths we can take so you have options to present to finance:

1) Price-hold + modest uplift (recommended)
   - 12-month extension, 10% list discount on committed units, 30% uplift in committed capacity starting 2027-10-01
   - 90-day price-hold on variable overages (protects you during migration to new usage patterns)
   - One-time bridge credit equivalent to 2% of ARR to cover migration spikes

2) Bigger discount, phased commit
   - 18-month term, 18% discount on committed units, staggered 15% commit increases at month 7 and 13
   - No price-hold on overages; overage rate reduced by 5% for first 6 months

3) Minimal term extension + true-up protection
   - 6-month extension to align to budget year, no discount, flexible true-up with capped rate increases (max +12% for year)

Attached are a term sheet and an updated SOW stub (Amaris_Renewal_Term_Sheets.pdf; SOW_Q2_2027_v3.docx) showing how each path maps to expected invoicing.

If you can share the primary constraint from your side (procurement requires multi-year commit vs finance wanting short-term holding pattern), I can prioritize the proposal and surface internal approvals.

Happy to get a short call on Wednesday if that helps.

Best,
Alex
Alex Martinez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0134
redwood.com

--
Attachment: Amaris_Renewal_Term_Sheets.pdf (3 pages, table of options)
Attachment: SOW_Q2_2027_v3.docx (workorder outline)
From: Tara Singh <tara@amarisplc.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: David Lin <david.lin@amarisplc.com>, Amaris Finance <finance@amarisplc.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris

Alex —

Thanks for the clear options. High level notes from our side after a quick run with procurement and finance:

- Procurement prefers a longer term (12–24 months) to lock pricing.
- Finance is comfortable with a small uplift in commit but needs an initial credit or discount to offset this year’s budget constraints — they asked whether a 10% one-time credit or a 5% effective discount across the term would be possible.
- We’re concerned about variable spend during the first quarter after the uplift — that 90-day price-hold looks attractive.

Short ask: can Redwood offer a blended option that combines a 12-month extension, a 12% effective discount (can be structured as a 10% list + 2% bridge credit), and a 2-month price-hold rather than 90 days? If we can get that, I can present to our CFO this afternoon.

Also, we need to see a sample amendment that includes language for a phased commit increase (we plan to ramp usage in stages).

Best,
Tara
Tara Singh | Head of AI Platform, Amaris PLC
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@amarisplc.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris

Tara —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can do a blended structure that lines up with procurement and finance asks. Proposed commercial summary:

- Term: 12 months (effective 2027-07-01 to 2028-06-30)
- Commit: +30% baseline uplift effective 2027-10-01, with two staged ramp checkpoints (2027-10-01 and 2028-01-01) to validate consumption and adjust capacity if needed
- Pricing: 10% standard discount on committed units + 2% one-time bridge credit applied on first invoice (equivalent to ~2% ARR) = 12% effective first-year concession
- Price-hold: 60 days (we can support 60 days firm; finance asked for 2 months in their note) on variable overage rates from go-live of uplift
- Implementation credit: one-time $Xk migration credit to offset spike charges (we proposed 2% ARR previously; final amount to be confirmed on deal math)

Next steps from our side: Monica will prepare an amendment draft including phased commit language and SOW changes; Laura will confirm final credit numbers and margin tolerance. Vivek and I will queue this for approvals so we can lock the amendment into DocuSign if you approve.

If this sounds aligned, I’ll send a near-final amendment and a single-page summary for your CFO.

Thanks —
Alex

--
Attachment: Amaris_Renewal_Term_Sheets.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris

Team —

Ran quick margin sims for the blended option. Short summary:

- 12% effective concession at the levels proposed keeps gross margin within acceptable band if the bridge credit is capped to 2% ARR (we should round to nearest $5k on the credit to simplify invoicing).
- 60-day price-hold on overages is doable but recommend we exclude third-party GPU pass-through costs from the hold (call that out in the amendment).
- Phased commit language: we should include a soft review at each checkpoint (30 days after ramp start) with a mutual measurement window and an optional stretch credit if Amaris materially exceeds forecast (>25% vs estimate).

I’m ok to sign off subject to final credit dollar amount and legal reviewing the amendment for pass-through exclusions. Monica — can you draft the amendment with those guardrails and set a 24-hour review window?

Laura
Laura Bennett | Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@amarisplc.com>, David Lin <david.lin@amarisplc.com>, Amaris Finance <finance@amarisplc.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract extension and pricing options — Amaris

Tara / David —

Following internal approvals, attached is the near-final amendment and a one-page commercial summary. Key points aligned to your ask: 12-month term, 10% list discount + 2% bridge credit applied on first invoice (12% effective), +30% commit uplift staged (2027-10-01 and 2028-01-01), 60-day hold on variable overage rates (excludes GPU pass-through), and a capped migration credit equivalent to 2% ARR rounded to nearest $5k.

I’ve also included DocuSign for the amendment here: https://www.docusign.com/prepare?envelopeId=0b8a9e-amaris-amend. If the terms are acceptable to your CFO, we can route for signature and target an effective date of 2027-07-01.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the CFO through the numbers.

Best,
Alex
